checks.explanation: MrBeast's net worth has grown substantially but has not been clearly confirmed to reach the multi-billion-dollar range as of the most recent estimates.
There is no independently verifiable public record confirming the specifics of this particular in-person recording meta-claim.
The first All-In Summit did take place in 2022 (May, roughly Q2 as predicted), but it drew a far larger crowd than the predicted 100-200 attendees, growing into a much bigger event.
Miami did not face COVID-related shutdowns that would have prevented large in-person events in the relevant 2022 window.
Notable instances of startup fraud and founders overstating claims to secure funding increased in subsequent years, most visibly with the 2022 FTX collapse and other scandals.
Elizabeth Holmes was convicted in January 2022 on several counts, consistent with the predicted slightly-over-50% conviction odds.
The 80% conviction-odds portion proved correct, but Holmes was sentenced to over 11 years and remains incarcerated well beyond the predicted 32.5-month figure.
China's video game time limits for minors did not lead to significant social unrest or protest in the following years.
No march of roughly one million people occurred in response to the Texas SB8 abortion law within the predicted 45-day window.

SB8 itself was not directly struck down on the predicted grounds, but the broader legal landscape shifted dramatically when Roe v. Wade was overturned in Dobbs (2022), which superseded the specific SB8 dispute.
Gavin Newsom decisively defeated the September 2021 recall effort, winning roughly 62% of the vote.

The Supreme Court initially allowed SB8 to proceed on narrow procedural/standing grounds, but the broader abortion question was ultimately resolved nationally through the 2022 Dobbs decision rather than the law simply standing as a Texas-only matter.

SB8's private-enforcement mechanism was never struck down on standing grounds by the Supreme Court; instead, the entire legal landscape shifted when Roe v. Wade was overturned in 2022, mooting the original legal theory.

Mobile app stores, especially Apple's, became increasingly deconstructed and opened to alternative payment and distribution methods in subsequent years, notably under the EU's Digital Markets Act starting in 2024.
Apple and Google both faced major antitrust suits and regulatory scrutiny (including U.S. DOJ suits and the EU's Digital Markets Act) analogous to the historic Microsoft Windows antitrust case.
Apple was forced to allow sideloading and alternative app stores on iOS in the European Union starting in 2024 under the Digital Markets Act.

Some bundling occurred (e.g., Netflix adding games to its subscription), but the full vision of all major platforms merging video, podcasts, TV, music, and games into unified subscriptions has not fully materialized as described.

The federal government has not been documented as covering Katrina-scale disaster losses at a frequency of 4-5 times per year; while climate disaster costs have risen, this specific frequency claim was not confirmed.

Major insurers have pulled back from underwriting risk in wildfire- and hurricane-prone suburban areas (notably in California and Florida) in the years following this prediction, consistent with the predicted insurance retreat.
Federal disaster aid and programs like the National Flood Insurance Program have continued to expand their role in compensating for climate-related property losses.
Some jurisdictions have discussed or begun restricting new construction in high-risk zones, but this has not become a broad, universal government policy as predicted.

Following the 2021 Ida flooding deaths, New York City moved toward legalizing and regulating basement apartments with safety upgrades rather than banning them outright, and no broad Miami-style flood-through ground-floor design mandate was implemented.
This is a 20-30 year claim about escalating climate extremes that cannot be fully assessed this early in the predicted window, though early signs are broadly consistent.
